Peter McDonald took miles out of his best 3000 metre time as he ran 9:24.3 (and still had the 'chase to come) and Joe Panton, always good for a low 52 400m, tried his hand at the two lap race and timed it to perfection as he turned on his speed in the finish straight to record a winning first ever attempt at the event.
Noel Levy (400m) and Jamie Webb again were our winners but Dotun Akinbogun shone in the 100m and non-scoring 400m where he and Joe Panton were neck and neck all down the finish straight.
Let's pay tribute to a couple of other men who always get near the front and who have contributed so much to the season's success — sprinters Dotun Akinbogun and Joe Panton.

Marlon Dickson ended the Rosenheim season as he had started, by winning the 100 metres, but here we must pay credit to all the sprinters — Richard David, James Hilston, Dotun Akinbogun, Joe Panton, Michael Peacock, Nick Molloy and others.

He sends his regards to coach Bob Bridges and his old training group, especially Nick Molloy, Dotun Akinbogun, Richard David, Richard Mcmillan, Joe Panton and James Hilston; also to John Jeffrey, Mike Small, Patricia and Alan Mead and of course his good friend Past President Ted Pallant.
